statement: A competent authority must form an opinion that the land is lawfully entitled to the State before issuing a quit notice under the State Lands (Recovery of Possession) Act.
supporting_quote: When one considers the detailed provisions of the Act, which has been outlined above, and the objective that is sought to be achieved, which is the expeditious recovery of State land from persons who are in unauthorised occupation of such State lands, it is the view of this Court that the Competent Authority is only required to form an opinion that the impugned land is land to which the State is lawfully entitled to, and that the possession or occupation is unauthorized.

statement: A land owner does not have a statutory right to demand the exercise of the power by the Minister to revoke a vesting order under Section 38 of the Land Acquisition Act No. 9 of 1950, as amended, where the possession of the land remains with the original landowner and the public purpose for which the land was acquired remains.
supporting_quote: It would therefore be totally inconsistent with the statutory scheme to contend that any of these provisions, section 50(1), 39(1) or 39A afford a statutory right to a person interested in the land to demand the exercise of such power by the Minister.

statement: A person who has objected to a proposed land acquisition under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act must be given an opportunity to present their position.
supporting_quote: When such objections are considered every objector shall be given an opportunity of being heard in support thereof

statement: A party can establish a right to a servitude by showing that the water naturally flows from the upper tenement to the lower tenement, and the lower proprietor is only obliged to receive such water as flows in the ordinary course of nature.
supporting_quote: Every owner of property is bound to receive the water which naturally drains onto his property from the land lying on a higher level than his own, nor may he raise any obstruction on his land whereby the water is dammed back on the property above him (Retief v. Louw, 4 Buch. p. 174; Ludolf v Wegner, 6 S.C. 193).

statement: Courts may order exemplary costs to be paid by a party for abusing the process of the court, as a punishment and to deter similar actions in the future.
supporting_quote: Thus, considering the conduct of the Petitioner and the fact that he has abused the process of Court by filing several applications in different Courts at different times without vacating from the land and premises in question for more than three years, we direct the Petitioner to pay a sum of Rs. 200, 000 as costs to the Director General, Sri Lanka Broadcasting Corporation within a period of one month from today...

statement: Administrative decisions must be made in accordance with due process and after considering all relevant facts, including any pending inquiries or proceedings.
supporting_quote: Unless that restriction on the power of the court is observed, the court will in my view, under the guise of preventing the abuse of power, be itself guilty of usurping power..... Judicial review, as the words imply, is not an appeal from a decision, but a review of the manner in which the decision was made.

statement: A co-owner who has been in possession of a land for a long period without interruption or disturbance is entitled to a share in the land, even if they do not have a clear title.
supporting_quote: The said Podisira Fernando died leaving Alawattage Jemis Fernando, and per averment 5 of the Amended Plaint it is said the that Alawattage Jemis had conveyed Y-t share of the land to a third party, which has been possessed by the 4th Defendant.

statement: A party can make submissions on the devolution of title of the parties to the action even at the appeal stage, and the court may order a re-trial if necessary.
supporting_quote: Merely because her claim was to have an exclusion of a particular portion of the corpus, she is not prevented from taking up the matters pertaining to the devolution of title of the parties to the action even at this appeal stage.

statement: A deed executed before the institution of the case and tendered to court must be accepted as a document by which a party became entitled to a share of the corpus.
supporting_quote: This deed 4D2 which gives rights to 10 perches of the corpus to the 4th Defendant has been tendered to court and I therefore hold that the Deed No.6182 marked as 4D2 must be accepted as a document by which the 4th Defendant became entitled to 10 perches and this 10 perches should be added to the 63/7560 shares already allotted to the 4th Defendant by the judgment entered in this case.

statement: A court in a partition action has the power to exclude a separate lot wrongly included by a plaintiff as part of the corpus, and to declare the owner of the separate lot in an interlocutory decree.
supporting_quote: In an action instituted under section 2 of the Partition Act to partition land the Court has inherent power, under section 839 of the Civil Procedure Code, to make an order excluding a separate or divided lot or land which has been wrongly included by the plaintiff as being part of the corpus

statement: A person who converts a strip of land into a roadway under a deed with a condition allowing others to use it as a right of way also grants that right to their successors and assigns.
supporting_quote: when she converted the said strip of land to a roadway according to the condition stated in the said deed , the plaintiff too became entitle to use the said road way and there is evidence to show that Henricus (vendee in deed No.10219) too exercised the said right to use the road way as a right of way.

statement: In a rei vindication action, the plaintiff must prove and establish his title to the land in suit.
supporting_quote: The burden is on the plaintiff-respondent to establish his title he pleaded and relied on by him. Admittedly the plaintiff-respondent has failed to prove and establish that he is the sole owner of the land in suit.

statement: A party invoking the provisions of section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance to defeat the ownership of an adverse claimant to immovable property must establish a starting point for their acquisition of prescriptive rights, which must be undisturbed, uninterrupted, adverse to or independent of that of the former possessor and must have lasted for at least ten years.
supporting_quote: According to section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance such a possession must be undisturbed, uninterrupted, adverse to or independent of that of the former possessor and should have lasted for at least ten years before he could transform such possession into prescriptive title.

statement: A trust can co-exist with unjust enrichment, and the court can consider both when determining the nature of a transaction.
supporting_quote: These two have I gone hand in hand in the instant case.

statement: A person who has been dispossessed of immovable property otherwise than by process of law can institute proceedings against the person dispossessing him at any time within one year of such dispossession.
supporting_quote: Section 4 of the Prescription Ordinance declares: ~

statement: A plaintiff must indicate whether the property to be partitioned is paraveni or acquired property in the plaint.
supporting_quote: He also has not disclosed the names of the illegitimate children in his plaint and had failed to give notice under section 20(1) of the Partition Law.

statement: The burden of proof is on the defendant in an action for declaration of title to property where the legal title is in the plaintiff but the property is in the possession of the defendant.
supporting_quote: In an action for declaration of title to property, where the legal title is in the Plaintiff but the property is in the possession of the Defendant, the burden of proof is on the Defendant - See. Siyaneris vs Jayasinghe Udenis de Silva 52 NLR 289(PC) .

statement: The trial judge must identify the land to be partitioned first, and if the parties are not in agreement about the identity of the corpus and boundaries, it is the duty of the court to identify the correct land.
supporting_quote: If the parties are not in agreement about the identity of the corpus and boundaries it is the duty of court to identify the correct land.

statement: A lessee or licensee must first restore the property to their landlord before disputing the title of the person who gave them the lease or license.
supporting_quote: In this case the defendant was permitted to occupy the premises with the permission of the Plaintiff. In my opinion the defendant has no defence to this action. He must give up possession to the Plaintiff.

statement: The burden of proof is on the defendant to show independent rights in the form of prescription when the plaintiff's paper title is undisputed.
supporting_quote: Once paper title became undisputed the burden shifted to the defendants to show that they had independent rights in the form of prescription as claimed by them

statement: A person who enters into possession of land without a valid title or license cannot claim undisputed possession against the vendors of the plaintiff.
supporting_quote: He undertook to handover peaceful possession if he defaults to buy. Hence, he cannot be heard to say that he is a licensee, but on the other hand, he is a trespasser against whom the Plaintiff has a right to institute this action.

statement: A plaintiff cannot unite two or more causes of action in the same case if they are not related.
supporting_quote: under Sec. 36 (1) of the Civil Procedure Code it could be done.

statement: A party who remains on the record without participating in the trial cannot be considered an aggrieved party.
supporting_quote: A party qua Appellants who missed the opportunity of availing himself of putting forward his case in the original court cannot be treated on par with a victim of an offence who is so desirous of taking advantage of Section 260 of the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No. 15 of 1979.

statement: A person who knows the value of the property is not entitled to rescission of the sale merely by reason of the fact that the price at which he has sold it, is less than half its true value.
supporting_quote: a person who knows the value of his property is not entitled to recession of the sale merely by reason of the fact that the price at which he had sold the property is less than half its true value .....

statement: A person who enters into possession of a land in one capacity is presumed to continue in possession in the same capacity, and a co-owner's possession in law is tantamount to the possession of his other co-owners.
supporting_quote: It is not possible for him to put an end to that possession by any secret intention in his mind unless there is proof of nothing short of ouster or something equivalent to ouster.
